text: Hi, I'm Lumo. I'm a moth. I know a thing or two about staring at bright screens.
This is my family's TV. It's the biggest screen in the house, and the hardest one to type on. Cheetah, one letter... at... a... time. Still going.

So we fixed it. Scan the code, and your phone becomes a keyboard and a touchpad. No app to install. Everyone gets a color, and the cursor wears the color of whoever moved it last. Maya types. Leo scrolls. Nobody fights over the remote.
Long pages are hard to read from the couch. Press Make it cards, and I turn the page into big field-guide cards the whole room can read. Want one read out loud? Here's my reading voice.
Now the fun part: family quests. Tonight it's Speed Safari. Find three animals faster than a car on the highway.
Everyone races on their own phone. Found one? Submit it, and I check the page with AWS. I don't just say yes. I show you the sentence that proves it.
A house cat? Nice try, Leo.
Golden eagle! That's three. Maya wins the safari.
Some nights, the room just drifts. Page, page, page. I know circling when I see it.
So I get a little sleepy, and I offer something better: a quest, or a curious detour.
Say we're fine, and I believe you. I just wait longer next time. I learn your household. I never nag.

How it works: phones talk to the TV over your own Wi-Fi. Page text leaves the TV only when you ask. Then, on AWS, API Gateway, Lambda, Bedrock with Guardrails, DynamoDB and Polly do the thinking. No network? I still work.
